sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Loads the libraries, icons, store, grade table, AI helper, voice input button and button component.
sections.why: Each piece supports either the form or the AI helper.
sections.watch_out: The AI helper sends text to an outside service.

sections.name: CourseModalProps
sections.title: Pop-up inputs
sections.what: Defines the parent's inputs: open state, close function, and an optional course to edit.
sections.why: Lets one pop-up handle both adding and editing.

sections.name: CourseModal (part 1)
sections.title: Form state and AI parsing
sections.what: Holds the field values, loads them from the course being edited or resets them to defaults when the pop-up opens, and runs the AI helper. The helper fills in any fields the AI returns and shows a success note.
sections.why: Lets the owner type one sentence instead of filling every field.
sections.watch_out: If the AI call fails, the owner gets no visible error and the fields stay as they were.

sections.name: CourseModal (part 2)
sections.title: Save and delete
sections.what: On submit, it skips blank code or name, then adds or updates the course with trimmed text, numbers and optional fields. Delete asks the owner to confirm and then removes the course.
sections.why: Keeps one save path for new and existing courses, and protects against accidental deletion.
sections.watch_out: Credits of 0 are saved as 4, and attendance of 0 is saved as 100.

sections.name: CourseModal (part 3)
sections.title: AI box and voice input
sections.what: Shows a highlighted box with a text field, a voice button, and an Auto-Fill button, plus a success note after the AI fills the fields.
sections.why: Puts the quick-entry option at the top of the form.
sections.watch_out: Pressing Enter in the box also triggers the AI, which can surprise someone who expects a plain text entry.

sections.name: CourseModal (part 4)
sections.title: Course code, name, credits and professor
sections.what: Shows the required course code and name fields, plus credits (1 to 12) and an optional professor field.
sections.why: These are the core identifying details of a course.

sections.name: CourseModal (part 5)
sections.title: Grade, attendance and delete button
sections.what: Shows a grade dropdown that includes an in-progress option, an attendance percent field, and a delete button only when editing.
sections.why: Records the outcome and attendance needed for the grade and dashboard displays.

sections.name: CourseModal (part 6)
sections.title: Cancel and save buttons
sections.what: Shows Cancel to close without saving, and a save button labeled Add Course or Save Changes.
sections.why: Gives the owner a clear way to finish or leave the form.

summary: A pop-up for adding or editing a course, with an AI helper that fills the fields from a sentence the owner types or speaks.
purpose: Lets the owner record each course's code, name, credits, professor, grade and attendance, and optionally fill these from plain language.
why: Courses feed the CGPA calculation and the semester views, so they need to be entered accurately and quickly.
how: When opened, the fields load either the course being edited or blank defaults. The AI helper sends the owner's sentence to the Groq AI provider and fills in any fields it returns. On save, values are trimmed and numbers are converted, then the course is added or updated in the store. A delete button asks for confirmation before removing the course.
inputs: Whether the pop-up is open, a function to close it, an optional course to edit, the owner's typed or spoken text, and the form fields.
outputs: Calls to add, update or delete a course in the store. The AI helper sends text to an outside service and receives suggested field values back.
risks: The owner's text leaves the app and goes to an outside AI service, so private details should not be typed there. If the AI call fails, the owner sees no message, only a console log. A default course code of CS-101 can be filled in as if it were real. Credits of 0 become 4 because of the fallback.
debug: If the AI helper does nothing, check the browser console for the logged parse error and confirm the Groq provider is configured. If a course is saved with odd values, check the fallback defaults in the save step. If the delete does nothing, the owner may have cancelled the confirmation.
